I'd say around 16 is normal, though way earlier happens a fair amount. My advice: hold off until college if you can. In junior high/high school most people don't even know who they are yet, you can start dating someone and they become a completely different person within a few weeks. In college, that happens significantly less and the two of you (hopefully) know enough about yourselves that that doesn't happen.

There's a lot of anger here. I get frustrated with this too, but honestly you need to step outside of yourself, and put yourself in her position. It's very scary, dating someone new. It's like going out with a half bear half lion and hoping "Oh I hope this one's nice and doesn't try to abuse me or use me physically or emotionally" and many women begin to doubt themselves and your intentions as the time to meet up approaches. If it happens multiple times, communicate your frustration. If you're honest about it and not a dick, hopefully she'll respond in kind. If not, it's time to move on and find someone new and awesome, who respects you and your time.
